chapters.summary: Kishkindha: Hanuman meets Rama with flawless speech, Rama and Sugriva become friends, and the vanaras search the south until Jambavan reminds Hanuman of his strength.

signs.text: Rishyamuka hill. The vanara Sugriva lives in hiding on its summit. Lake Pampa lies below.
Kishkindha, the cave city of the vanaras. Throne hall to the north, shrine to the north-west.
Mahendra hill, above the southern ocean.

cmds.say: Following Shabari's directions, Rama and Lakshmana walk along Lake Pampa toward the hill {n:place.rishyamuka}.
Rama still grieves for Sita, but the lotus lake and the birdsong lift his heart a little.
Shabari said the vanara Sugriva hides on this hill. He will help us find her.

cmds.objective: Climb Rishyamuka hill and find Sugriva.

cmds.say: These are the shores of Pampa. Shabari served the sages here all her life.
The vanaras on the hill above watch every traveller. Walk peacefully and they will come to you.
A wandering mendicant comes down the path, bows, and greets the princes in a gentle voice.
Who are you, radiant ones, walking these hills with bows in your hands and bark garments on your shoulders? Sugriva, king of the vanaras, sent me to ask.

then.choice: The mendicant asks you: "Who are these two?"

options.label: We are going up to see Sugriva.
Rama and Lakshmana, the sons of King Dasharatha.

then.say: Sugriva himself sent me here. But first tell me: who are they?
From Ayodhya! But who are they?
The sons of Dasharatha! Then my king will be glad to meet them.

cmds.say: His words are clear, measured and sweet. Rama turns to Lakshmana in wonder.
Listen to how he speaks, Lakshmana. No one could speak like this without having learned the Vedas.
And surely he has studied the whole of grammar, again and again. He has said so much, yet not one word was wrong.
Rama praises {w:vyakarana} itself! Your verse book glows: this is the key verse of Kishkindha.

onCorrect.say: Exactly. Words joined by sandhi come apart cleanly when you know the rules.

onWrong.say: Not quite. Sandhi joins words at their edges; learn the split and the words appear.

cmds.say: You honour me, prince. Forgive my disguise. I am Hanuman, son of the Wind, minister to Sugriva.
Your young companion carries a book of verses. Let us test words together, friend, so I can tell my king what kind of people you are.

then.say: Let us play a game of verses, friend: a chain of lines.
I say a line. You answer with a line that begins with my line's last sound.

battle.intro: Hanuman invites you to a friendly contest of verses.

then.say: A fine chain! You know the verses line by line.

onWin.say: Your words ring true, and your heart is honest. I am persuaded.
He takes his true form, mighty as a hill, and lifts both princes onto his shoulders to carry them to his king.

onWin.objective: Follow the path up to Sugriva on the hilltop.

onLose.say: Well argued, but not yet convincing.

cmds.say: Gather your thoughts, friend, and speak with me again when you are ready.
Shall we test words again, friend? Speak, and I will listen.

battle.intro: Hanuman smiles and waits for your verse.

onWin.say: Your words ring true, and your heart is honest. I am persuaded.
He takes his true form and lifts both princes onto his shoulders to carry them to his king.

onWin.objective: Follow the path up to Sugriva on the hilltop.

cmds.say: Rest a while, and we will speak again.
Halt! Two strangers with bows climb toward our king.
Only Hanuman, our wise minister, may bring strangers before Sugriva. He went down the path to meet you.

then.say: Our king has a friend at last. The whole hill feels lighter.

else.say: King Sugriva has lived in fear since his brother Vali drove him out of Kishkindha.

then.say: The path behind me leads down through a cave to Kishkindha. Go with our king.

else.say: I am Nila. Speak with our king, and may this day bring good fortune.

then.say: Sugriva welcomes the princes warmly and offers Rama his hand.
Rama clasps his hand. Then Hanuman brings fire, and it burns between them.

else.say: Sugriva welcomes the princes warmly. Hanuman kindles a fire between two stones.

cmds.say: Rama and Sugriva walk around the fire together and swear friendship, with the fire as their witness.
Friend, some days ago we saw a lady carried through the sky by Ravana. She cried out, 'Rama! Lakshmana!'
She dropped these jewels, wrapped in her upper cloth. We have kept them safe.
Rama presses the jewels to his heart and weeps. He asks Lakshmana whether he knows them.
I do not know the {w:keyura}, nor the {w:kundala}. But the {w:nupura} I know, for every day I bowed at her feet.

onCorrect.say: Right! Lakshmana's devotion shows in every word of this verse.

onWrong.say: Not quite. Look again at the word card, then the meaning will stay with you.

cmds.say: My brother Vali drove me from Kishkindha and took everything I had. I live here only because he cannot climb this hill.

then.say: But Vali is mighty. Can anyone defeat him?
Seven great sala trees stand in a row. Rama takes up his bow and a single arrow.
In a moment the arrow flies back to Rama. Sugriva stares, amazed.

cmds.say: Rama promised to help his friend. In time, Sugriva regained his kingdom, and he vowed in turn to search the whole earth for Sita.

then.say: Vali fell to Rama's arrow. Before he died, he gave his son Angada this advice.

cmds.say: Sugriva joins your party!

cmds.objective: Take the cave path north to Kishkindha.

cmds.say: A dark cave leads north into the mountain. The vanaras on the hilltop should be met first.
{n:place.kishkindha_caves}: a city of caves and gardens, bright with torches and flowers.

then.say: The rains came. Rama waited on a nearby hill, thinking of Sita.
The rains passed, and the city celebrated its king.

else.say: The rains came and went. Rama waited out the monsoon on a nearby hill while the city celebrated its king.

cmds.say: When autumn cleared the skies, Sugriva called the vanara armies together.

cmds.objective: Go to Sugriva's council in the throne hall.

then.say: The southern party waits for us. Have you restored the verse at the shrine?

else.say: I am Angada, son of Vali. The vanara chiefs are gathered. My uncle the king will speak.
Search parties, go east, west and north! Search every forest, river and cave. Return within one month.
Angada will lead the south, with Hanuman, and Jambavan, king of the bears.
An old bear with a white mane steps forward and bows to Rama.
Jambavan joins your party!
Rama takes Hanuman aside and gives him his ring, engraved with his name.
If you find her, give her this. She will know you come from me.

else.objective: Restore the verse of perfect speech at the north-west shrine, then head east.

then.say: The verse of perfect speech shines gold. A messenger with such words cannot fail.

else.say: Welcome to the shrine of Kishkindha. Rest here whenever you are weary.
Hanuman's flawless speech moved Rama himself. Recite that verse with me, so its words return whole to your verse book.

then.say: The verse glows gold! Your recitation is as clear as Hanuman's speech.
A new mantra wakes in you: {n:move.shuddha_vak}. It strengthens the whole party.

then.objective: Leave Kishkindha by the east tunnel with the southern search party.

else.objective: Go to Sugriva's council in the throne hall.

else.say: Almost. A few words slipped. Rest a moment, then recite with me again.

cmds.say: Fruit from the forest, roots, honey and herbs! Stock up before the search.

then.say: Everyone is talking about Hanuman! Rama said he must have studied the whole of grammar, many times over.
In all Hanuman said, not one word came out wrong. That is {w:vyakarana}: every word in its right form.

cmds.say: Mangoes, jackfruit, rose-apples! Kishkindha has the sweetest fruit in the world.
Is it true that Hanuman jumped at the sun when he was a baby? He thought it was a ripe fruit!
My husband goes north with the search party. We will all look for Rama's queen.
Our new king forgot his promise during the rains, and Lakshmana came to the gate in fury. Queen Tara calmed him.
Now Sugriva keeps his word. A true friend remembers.

then.say: The east tunnel leads to the Vindhya forests. Go well, southern party!

else.say: The east tunnel leads out to the Vindhya forests.

cmds.say: The south tunnel goes back to Rishyamuka hill.

then.say: A messenger's words must be flawless. Let us restore the verse of perfect speech at the shrine before we go.

then.objective: Restore the verse of perfect speech at the north-west shrine.

else.say: Sugriva has not sent out the search parties yet. Meet his council in the throne hall.

cmds.say: The southern party combs the Vindhya forests, caves and rivers. Weeks pass with no sign of Sita.

cmds.objective: Search south-east through the Vindhya forest.

then.say: Rest, children of the forest. Then go on with your search.
Your party is fully rested.

else.say: Lost in a great cave, the hungry vanaras found a shining grove and a holy woman in bark garments.
I am Svayamprabha, keeper of this place. Eat, drink, and rest. Then close your eyes, and I will lead you out.
Your party is fully rested.

cmds.say: The month the king gave us is almost over, and we have found nothing.
If we return empty-handed, Sugriva will be angry. Some of us want to give up.

then.say: Sita is in Lanka! Come, to Mahendra hill. From there we will see the ocean.

else.say: The month is over. We reached the sea and found nothing. I would rather fast here than return in shame.

then.say: Go to Mahendra, children. Lanka lies a hundred yojanas to the south.

else.say: At the edge of the sea the vanaras sit in despair. Angada speaks of Jatayu, who gave his life defending Sita.
An old vulture with burnt wings drags himself out from the rocks.
Jatayu? Who speaks of my younger brother? Tell me how he died.

then.choice: Sampati asks: "How did my brother die?"

options.label: He fought Ravana to save Sita, and Ravana struck him down.

then.say: I heard the prince, child. But how did my brother die?
In the forest... But how? Tell me how.
Alas, my brother! He was a hero.

else.say: Long ago I flew too near the sun to shield him, and my wings burned away. But my eyes are still the sharpest in the world.
I saw Ravana carry a lady crying 'Rama! Lakshmana!' She is held in Lanka, an island a hundred yojanas across this ocean, in Ravana's garden.
Hope returns to the vanaras. They cheer and leap among the rocks.

else.objective: Go east to Mahendra hill above the ocean.

cmds.say: The trail leads toward a great hill by the sea. But where would we go? We must keep searching.
The vanaras reach the shore of the vast ocean. Its waves roar like a living thing.
Who can leap a hundred yojanas? One by one, the vanaras say how far they could jump.

then.objective: Ask each vanara how far he can leap.

else.objective: Climb to Angada on the clifftop.

cmds.say: I can leap ten yojanas. Not one more!

then.say: Every vanara has spoken. None can leap a hundred yojanas.

then.objective: Climb to Angada on the clifftop.

cmds.say: Twenty yojanas, perhaps. The ocean is so wide...

then.say: Every vanara has spoken. None can leap a hundred yojanas.

then.objective: Climb to Angada on the clifftop.

cmds.say: Thirty yojanas for me. Still not enough.

then.say: Every vanara has spoken. None can leap a hundred yojanas.

then.objective: Climb to Angada on the clifftop.

then.choice: Mainda asks: "How many yojanas is it from here to Lanka?"

options.label: A hundred yojanas. Sampati said so.
It lies to the south, on the far shore of the sea.

then.say: To the south, yes. But how many yojanas?

cmds.say: Sixty yojanas, if the wind is kind. But Lanka is a hundred away.

then.say: Every vanara has spoken. None can leap a hundred yojanas.

then.objective: Climb to Angada on the clifftop.

then.say: The summit is just above us. Go, Hanuman. All our hopes go with you.
First hear every vanara: how far can each one leap?

else.say: I could leap a hundred yojanas, but I am not sure I could come back. Who among us can do it?
In my youth I could have crossed it. Now I am old.
Jambavan turns to Hanuman, who sits apart, silent.
Why are you silent, Hanuman? You are the son of the Wind, as swift as Garuda.
As a child you leapt toward the rising sun, thinking it was a fruit. Because of a sage's curse you forgot your strength, until someone reminds you.
I remind you now. Rise, Hanuman! Cross the ocean and find Sita!

then.say: Hanuman rises. The vanaras praise him, and with every word of praise he grows.
He grows as vast as a mountain, and roars with joy.

else.say: Hanuman rises. He grows and grows, as vast as a mountain, and the vanaras roar with joy.
Hanuman remembers his true strength! He returns to your side stronger than ever.
I will leap from the peak of Mahendra. I will find Sita, or I will not return without news.

else.objective: Climb to the summit of Mahendra and leap: Book 5 begins there.

cmds.say: The summit of Mahendra. The vanaras below have not yet chosen who will leap.
An old chest sits in the corner of the clearing. Some earlier search party left fruit for the next.
You found 3 fruits.
A vanara search party, this far south? Ravana will reward me for your tails!

battle.intro: A night-wanderer springs out of the grass!

onWin.say: The night-wanderer flees into the forest, dropping a pouch of roots.

then.say: Hanuman sits apart, silent, looking out over the sea.
